name: Voxel Cube World
summary: A bright MagicaVoxel-style miniature world: every object is a real 3D cube grid, baked to sprites under one warm afternoon sun.
description: Characters, props, collectibles, particles and even HUD icons are small 3D voxel grids that a tiny software renderer turns into sprites once at startup: 3/4 orthographic view at 46 degrees, three face tones, per-voxel colour jitter and ambient occlusion. Characters are voxel rigs: every pose re-assembles legs, cloak hem, sleeves, scarf tail and head on whole-voxel offsets, so walks, breathing, blinks, lunges, hit poses and block break-ups stay snappy and grid-true. The ground is a flat field of 4x4-unit voxel tiles with one-voxel height steps, calm colour patches, clumped tufts and leaf litter under every crown. It reads like a tabletop toy diorama: saturated autumn colours, chunky shapes, no outlines.
avoidFor: projects needing many free-rotating 3D camera angles

difficulty.why: New assets are 3D cube grids that can be described very precisely in code with a few box() and blob() calls; the renderer adds light, ambient occlusion and shadows automatically. Effort grows only for very large or many-frame models, which take longer to build and bake.

technique.renderer: Canvas 2D (procedural, no image assets) with a built-in software voxel renderer that bakes sprites at init
technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites are baked at K = round(screenH/360*4)/4 (clamped 1.5–4) sprite px per world unit, with PPV = max(3, round(K*1.9)) px per voxel, so one voxel is ~1.9–2 world units. Ground chunks are rendered per pixel at up to 2.5 px per unit; blits are snapped to whole screen pixels.
technique.summary: Every object is a Uint16 voxel grid (x right, y toward the viewer, z up). At init each grid is rotated by a yaw (±0.6 rad for characters), projected orthographically with a 46° pitch, its exposed faces sorted back-to-front and filled as quads with 3 tones, jitter and AO, giving MagicaVoxel-looking sprites for 2 facings × all animation frames.
technique.linework: No outlines at all. Form is separated purely by face tones (top 1.0, sun-facing side ~0.88, shadow side ~0.68) and by dark 'carved' voxels painted on the front surface (e.g. #8a3412 rim around a glowing face). Faces are grown by 0.8 sprite px to hide hairline seams.
technique.shading: Three flat face tones per voxel: top = 1.0 and warmed (r×1.035, g×1.015, b×0.965); side tone = 0.76 − 0.15 × (screen-x of the rotated normal), so the left-facing side is ~0.88 and the right-facing side ~0.68, and sides are cooled toward blue. Each voxel's brightness is jittered ±4.5% by a hash. Each solid neighbour around an open face subtracts 7.5% (AO); side faces of the bottom layer get ×0.9.
technique.lighting: One fixed warm sun from the upper left (west). Cast shadows are blocky footprints sheared by (0.62, 0.26) per unit of height toward the lower right, blurred 0.16×PPV px, drawn at 42% alpha. Emissive voxels (carved faces, cracks, eyes, lamps) skip shading and get an additive radial glow sprite. A purple radial vignette and a faint warm top gradient finish the frame.
technique.texture: No texture maps. Variation comes from per-voxel hash jitter, random colour picks per voxel inside a material (2–4 shades), and on the ground per-tile colour picks from 4–7 shades plus a 1-px lit/dark tile bevel.

paletteRules: Bright, saturated mid-tones only: no pure black anywhere in the world; the darkest world colours are carved/hole voxels (#1c2044, #24122c, #2c221e).
Every material is 2–4 close shades picked per voxel by a hash, never one flat colour.
Warm sunlit tops, cool bluish sides: shading shifts hue, not just brightness.
Glowing parts (faces, cracks, eyes, lamps) are emissive voxels in yellow/orange plus an additive glow; they are the only things that glow.
Creatures are purple/white against a green/grey/brown world; the main character is orange + navy + teal so it pops on every ground type.
UI uses a separate dark-purple family (#2b2446 / #151024) with gold text so it never blends into the bright world.

world.summary: A flat infinite voxel terrain baked per 256-unit chunk, pixel by pixel: 4×4-unit tiles, each with a material (grass, leaf litter, field, stone, path, water) and a height (-1 water, 0 field/path, 1 normal, 2 raised). Where the tile to the north is higher, its side face is painted into the top of the lower tile, so the world looks like a stepped voxel diorama seen from above.
layers: Base: per-tile colour from the material's shade list picked by noise at two scales (64 and 22 units) with only 10 % hash salt, so tones form calm patches instead of speckle; ×(0.95–1.05) macro brightness noise
Tile bevel: top/left 0.42-unit strip ×1.035/×1.015, bottom/right ×0.95/×0.965 (stone joints ×0.86 / ×1.05)

Height steps: lit top edge (north colour ×1.14 + 6), grass lip (×0.8, 1.05 units), side face band of 1.9 units per height step in the material's side colour fading ×0.98→0.78, then a 0.9-unit contact shadow ×0.84
Sun shadow of west neighbours: 1.5-unit strip ×0.8 on lower tiles east of a higher tile

Decals with intent on a 7-unit jittered grid: grass tufts gather in clumps (noise/46 > 0.6), flowers grow in single-colour patches (noise/80 > 0.7), pebbles are rare; 16 crown-coloured leaf voxels lie under every tree (shadow side), loose leaves and twigs only sparsely on the leaf floor; sprouts in fields, moss/cracks on stone, lily pads and shore reeds on water
Per frame: blinking water glints (#e8f8ff), a warm additive light pool (60×30 units, alpha 0.14) under the main character

characters.summary: Characters are voxel rigs at ~2 world units per voxel: parts (legs, cloak, hem, sleeves, scarf tail, head) are boxes and super-ellipsoid blobs re-assembled for every pose on whole-voxel offsets, with faces painted onto the front-most voxel of each column. The main character is a pumpkin-headed figure in a navy cloak with a gold buckle and a teal scarf (12×12×22 voxels, 16 poses: 8 walk, 4 breathing idle, blink, dash crouch, dash lunge, hurt). Creatures: a purple-and-cream root creature in two designed variants (round with a three-leaf tuft, or tall with one whipping sprout, a lopsided eye, a fang and a root tail), a white spirit with a curling tail, alternating arm strokes and a trailing wisp, and a big plum root creature with glowing cracks that stomps; each has 6 walk poses + 1 hit pose. Every pose is baked for yaw +0.6 (facing right) and -0.6 (facing left), so the model really turns instead of being mirrored.
rules: Big head on a readable body: the pumpkin head is 10×9×8 voxels on a 4-voxel cloak and 2-voxel legs; creatures are one big blob with tiny legs and one or two features (leaf tuft, sprout + root tail, wisp, crack lines).

Animation = re-posing on whole voxels: legs step ±1–3 voxels and lift 1 in the swing phase, the body bobs 1 voxel at passing, arms counter-swing, the head bob and the hem, scarf tail and leaves lag one frame behind (follow-through).
Small creatures waddle: the body shifts 1 voxel over the stance foot, hops 1 voxel at passing and squashes (z −0.35, x +0.25) at contact.
Every creature has a hit pose (squashed, leaves flung up, eyes squeezed to > < or widened) used while the flash is above 0.25.

Faces are 1-voxel pixels on the front surface: emissive yellow with a dark carved rim (#8a3412) for a warm glowing face, emissive red eyes (#ff4a2c) and dark brows for menacing creatures, dark holes (#1c2044) for ghosts; the main character blinks (eyes become one-voxel slits).
No outlines and no mirroring; separate yaw renders keep the light from the left on both facings.
Every character casts a blocky blurred shadow to the lower right (alpha 0.42; floating figures 0.22, drawn at alpha 0.86 hovering 1.6–4.6 units).

props.summary: Scenery objects are voxel grids with the same 2-unit voxel and the same upper-left sun as the characters, each baked at one fixed yaw (−0.4 to 0.6) with its own blocky shadow and y-sorted with the characters: autumn trees, pines, pumpkins, hay bales, crates, gravestones, lamp posts, fences, bushes, mossy rocks and mushrooms.
rules: Deciduous tree 15×15×24: 3×3 bark trunk (#7a5236 / #5f3f29), crown of one big p=3.2 blob + 4 random p=3 blobs + a top blob, in orange (#f08a2c…), red (#df4c34…) or yellow (#f0c03e…) colour sets of 4 shades.
Pine 13×13×25: 5 stacked tiers of p=2.6 discs shrinking upward (radii 6.2→1.5), #2f6e4c with #255a3e tier bottoms and 20% #3d8659 speckle.

Small props: pumpkin 8×8×8 / 11×11×10 (optionally carved with an emissive face and a small glow), hay bale 10×9×9 (#ebc75c), crate 6×6×6 (#b07a46 with #7c5230 edges where ≥ 2 coordinates are on the border), gravestone 7×3×10 with engraved cross and moss, lamp post 5×5×15 with emissive glass #ffcf5a, fence 13×1×6, bush with 7% red berry voxels #e2423a, mossy rock, red-capped mushroom.
Every prop uses 2–4 hashed shades per material and the ±4.5% jitter, never one flat colour; no outlines.
Props cast the same sheared sun shadow as characters, drawn at alpha 0.40.
Props stand only where the tile and the tile to the south share material and height — never on steps, water or paths.
Tall props (trees, pines) fade to alpha 0.45 when the main character is behind them.
Glowing props (lamp posts, carved pumpkins) add a warm additive glow (radius 14 / 7 units, alpha 0.5 ± 0.08).

effects.name: Core flash
effects.how: A voxel plus-burst (centre block + 4 arms, a 3×3 block from step 2) in the burst colour with a white centre voxel, growing in whole-voxel steps (1–4) over 0.12–0.22 s – the first layer of hits, bursts, pickups and celebrations.

effects.name: Cube debris
effects.how: Impacts and bursts spawn 2–34 tiny 1-voxel cubes (pre-rendered in 6 yaw frames, no AO) in the palette of the object that bursts; vz 60–140, gravity 320, drag 1.4, they tumble through the 6 frames, bounce, shrink to 60 % while resting and leave a small square shadow. Ghost cubes float up; the large creature also throws dirt cubes.

effects.name: Square rings
effects.how: Shockwaves are filled 4-sided frames squashed by sin(46°) whose radius grows in whole-voxel steps (outQuad 6→24, 10→48, 8→54 units), width shrinking with the life; big bursts stagger a second ring 0.1–0.12 s later. Never circles.

effects.name: Block break-up
effects.how: A vanishing creature swells one voxel and whites out (14 %), then its hit pose is sliced into 3×4 rectangular blocks (4×5 for the large creature) that fly out and up, tumble in eighth-turn steps, land and rest on the ground, and fade after 55 %; a white copy fades over the first 35 %. Spirits float up and shrink instead. At most 8 per frame.

effects.name: Stack-up appearance
effects.how: Creatures are built from the ground up in whole voxel layers (PPV·cos46° px, outQuad over the first 75 %) while 5 dirt cubes (#8c5b37, #a87a4c, #6fae46) pop out, then land with a bounce (stretch 1.1, squash 0.93); spirits form from the top down with a 26 Hz flicker.

effects.name: Residue tiles
effects.how: Where something burst, 3–5 dark tiles (#4a2a5e, #3a2a40, #9fc4ee) snapped to a 3-unit ground grid fade in over 0.12 s and out over the last 45 % of 0.9–2 s.

effects.name: Emissive bloom
effects.how: Additive (lighter) radial gradient sprite over carved faces (alpha 0.34 ± 0.06 flicker, dimmed during a blink), lamps, lanterns and glowing cracks.

effects.name: Projectile, collectibles, lanterns
effects.how: A spinning 3×2×4 voxel seed with three trailing squares; stepped voxel octahedra (mint 5×5×7, gold 7×7×10) in 8 spin frames hovering in half-voxel steps with a hold at the top and bottom; small purple-and-cream root lanterns with an emissive carved face orbiting with a warm glow.

atmosphere.summary: One warm afternoon sun from the upper left is baked into every voxel face and every shadow; the only runtime light is additive glow on emissive parts. A soft purple radial vignette and a faint warm wash at the top frame the bright diorama. No bloom pass, no grading, no grain.
rules: Face tones: top 1.0 warmed (r×1.035, b×0.965); sides 0.76 − 0.15·R(n).x and cooled toward blue; AO −7.5% per solid neighbour around an open face.

Cast shadows: voxel footprints at z and z+1 sheared (0.62, 0.26) per unit of height to the lower right, filled black, blurred 0.16·PPV px, 0.62 layer alpha + 0.55 contact layer for z ≤ 1.5; drawn at 0.42 (characters), 0.40 (props), 0.22 (floating figures).
Small collectibles, orbiting objects and projectiles use a flat dark #1d2a14 rectangle at 0.22–0.28 alpha instead of a baked shadow.
Ground steps: lit top edge ×1.14 + 6, side bands darkening ×0.98 → ×0.78, 0.9-unit contact strip ×0.84, 1.5-unit sun shadow ×0.8 east of higher tiles.

Glow sprite: 64 px radial gradient (0.9 → 0.35 → 0 alpha) in warm rgb(255,190,80), mint rgb(120,255,200), gold rgb(255,200,80) or hot rgb(255,150,50), drawn with lighter compositing; only emissive voxels glow.
Ground light: only a 60×30-unit warm pool under the main character (alpha 0.14) and blinking water glints #e8f8ff.

Vignette: radial gradient centred at (w/2, 0.48h), inner radius 0.32h, outer 0.62w, rgba(30,20,60,0) → 0.6: rgba(30,20,60,.12) → rgba(24,14,50,.42); plus a warm wash rgba(255,236,190,.10) at the top fading out by 35%.
Overlay screens dim the world with radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 45%, rgba(40,30,80,.35), rgba(16,10,34,.78)).
No outlines, bloom pass, colour grading or film grain; darker moods come from more emissive voxels and glows, not a darker renderer.

Ambient motion, slower than the actors: single leaf voxels in the autumn colours flutter down over the leaf floor (one per other 56-unit cell, 5–8 s fall, height and drift snapped to half voxels, flipping between a wide and a tall rectangle), water glints blink on pond tiles.

ui.summary: Chunky 'voxel slab' UI: flat dark-purple panels with a 3 px near-black edge, a hard 6 px drop edge below and inset hard highlights/shadows instead of gradients. Bars are segmented with 3 px dark gaps every 18 px and have 3 hard colour bands (highlight / main / shade). Bungee numbers carry stacked hard drop shadows that look extruded; icons are the same voxel models rendered at icon size (fitted to 84% of the box) with a dark offset silhouette shadow; cards use a two-tone #3d335f / #30284c background and gold split number keys.

motion: Everything moves in whole voxels and whole frames – poses are stepped, positions of effects snap to the voxel grid; that is what makes it read as a toy.

Main character walk: 8 poses, frame = floor(anim·3.2) mod 8; legs step [2,1,0,−1,−2,−1,0,1] voxels (the other leg mirrored), the swing foot lifts 1 voxel, the body bobs up 1 voxel at passing, arms counter-swing ±1, head bob, cloak hem (1–2 voxels back) and scarf tail lag one frame.
Idle: 4 held breathing poses 0.45 s each (head drops 1 voxel on the exhale, hem and scarf settle, hands rise 1), plus a blink pose for 0.14 s every 3.4 s.

Dash: crouch pose for the first 45 ms (body 1 voxel lower, legs split, arms back = anticipation), then the lunge (legs ±3 voxels, airborne +1, hem 3 voxels back, scarf streaming) with two orange after-images snapped to whole voxels.
Hurt: hurt pose while hurtT > 0.62 (~130 ms: hands up, head thrown back, eyes > <, mouth open) with a red tint.

Creatures: 6 poses + hit pose. Small creature: frame floor(anim·2.7) mod 6 (~10 fps, on-twos feel); large creature floor(anim·1.95) mod 6 with a 1-voxel body drop on each footfall; ghost floor(t·9 + seed·6) mod 6 hovering on an eased, stepped triangle wave. Per-actor phase comes from each actor's own counter or seed.
Hit: hit pose + white flash while flash > 0.25, knocked 1 voxel in the push direction for the first half, squash 1.08 × 0.93.
Collectibles spin through 8 yaw frames and hover in half-voxel steps; orbiting lanterns pick their spin frame from the orbit angle; floating numbers pop 0.6→1.15 in the first 12 % of life.
do: Model everything — props, collectibles, particles, icons — as voxel grids and bake them through the same renderer so lighting is identical.
Build characters as rigs: re-assemble the parts per pose on whole-voxel offsets and let hem, scarf, head and leaves lag one frame behind.
Give every state a pose: walk (8), idle breathing (4) + blink, crouch → lunge, hurt; creatures 6 walk + hit.
Keep one voxel ≈ 2 world units and bake two yaws (±0.6 rad) per pose instead of mirroring.
Colour materials by region and role (top/crown, zig-zag border, belly) and keep per-voxel jitter subtle; pick ground tones from noise patches.
Place decals where something causes them: litter under crowns, tufts in clumps, flowers in single-colour patches.
Make effects from cubes, plus-shaped flashes, stepped square rings and residue tiles.
dont: Don't add outlines or black strokes – voxel faces define the forms.
Don't interpolate poses smoothly or rotate sprites freely – motion is stepped (except tumbling debris in eighth turns).
Don't speckle: random per-voxel colour picks across a whole region read as noise.
Don't scatter tufts and flowers evenly over the grass.
Don't mix voxel sizes: a 1-unit-voxel prop next to 2-unit-voxel characters breaks the miniature scale.
Don't use circular rings or round particles; effects are square rings, plus-shaped flashes and cubes.
Don't use muted/dark palettes for the world; the look depends on bright, sunlit toy colours.
performance: All voxel rendering happens once in init(): 16 main-character poses + 4 creature sets × 7 poses (two small-creature variants), × 2 yaws, spin sets, ~15 props, debris cubes and shadows – a few hundred ms. Per frame everything is drawImage of cached canvases; break-ups draw 12–20 source-rect slices per creature (no clipping) and are capped at 8 per frame. Props are memoised per chunk so the ground can place leaf litter under neighbouring crowns. The expensive part stays the per-pixel ground chunk, built by a generator over several frames.
